definitions.explanation: A light snack or treat eaten between meals, traditionally in the afternoon. Originally referred to eating at the eighth hour (yatsu) of the traditional Japanese clock, around 2-3 PM.

examples.japanese: おやつ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧だ⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
{子|こ}どもたち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧おやつ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}した→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧。
examples.english: I prepared snacks for the children.

examples.japanese: ⟦{遠足|えんそく}→遠足：04107_ensoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧おやつ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧300⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{決|き}まっている→決まる：01233_kimaru⟧。
examples.english: There's a rule that snacks for the field trip can cost up to 300 yen.

notes:
USAGE:
A warm, everyday word used especially with children. The phrase ⟦{遠足|えんそく}→遠足：04107_ensoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧おやつ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧300⟦{円|えん}→円：00774_en⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧ is a nostalgic cultural reference — many Japanese people remember this rule from elementary school field trips. The word comes from {八|や}つ{時|どき} (the traditional time division for roughly 2-3 PM).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おやつ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時間|じかん}→時間：00468_jikan⟧ (snack time)
- おやつ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ (to eat a snack)
- おやつ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧ (to buy snacks)
- 3⟦{時|じ}→時：09869_ji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧おやつ (three o'clock snack)
